Next steps (suggested):
1) Please send the vendor questionnaire (we can take the attached version you referenced on the call). I attached a blank workbook labeled "ACME_Security_Questionnaire-v1.xlsx" to my calendar invite — attaching here as requested.
2) I'll loop in our security lead to confirm SOC 2 status and to provide a copy of the report/address any questions.
3) We'll provide a short tech note on how EU-region hosting works, what we store/transfer by default, and options for Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) for ITAR workloads.

Could you confirm target timeline for procurement review? Also, flag any specific export-control clauses (ITAR/OFAC) in your questionnaire so we can map answers.

Thanks — talk soon.

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap and for the questionnaire stub — sending the full questionnaire attached (updated). A couple of clarifications from our side before we send to procurement: 

- SOC 2: we need the most recent Type II (preferably 2025), and any carve-outs or scope limitations documented.
- EU region: confirm whether data-at-rest and KV cache never leaves EU region for hosted deployments. If there are background telemetry/logging endpoints, list where they route.
- Cross-border transfer: we need to know if any model components, model updates, or embeddings could be replicated to non-EU regions automatically.
- OFAC/ITAR: AcmeHealth will mark some projects ITAR-sensitive — does Redwood provide a Private deployment option that can be air-gapped / confined to on-prem or a dedicated VPC without any outbound replication?

Procurement would like answers within 3 business days if possible. I've attached our completed questionnaire (ACME_Security_Questionnaire-v1.xlsx) with sections highlighted in yellow where we need evidence.

Anna — thanks, received the completed questionnaire. Looping in Neha and Vivek from our sales/security ops teams to get definitive answers and the SOC 2 artifact.

Internal ask for Neha/Vivek: can you confirm the following items for the questionnaire and procurement: 
- Does Redwood have an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II covering the inference platform (2025)? If so, can we provision a redacted PDF for AcmeHealth and call out any scope limitations?
- For Hosted EU region: is data-at-rest (model weights excluded) and KV cache strictly kept in EU GCP region by default? Any telemetry endpoints that could reach a non-EU host?
- Are model updates or snapshots ever promoted to non-EU replicas automatically? If replication can occur for availability, can we provide an assurance or opt-out?
- For ITAR/OFAC: confirm Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) and whether we support an air-gapped install for ITAR-sensitive workloads. Also note any contractual/export-control steps we require (e.g., export classification assessments).

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Security Ops <sec-ops@acmehealth.eu>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency & export controls — follow-up from discovery call

Hi all — quick answers and artifacts attached/linked below. Happy to hop on a short call if Acme wants deeper detail.

1) SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report for 2025 that covers the inference hosting control environment. I've uploaded the redacted report here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/ACME/SOC2_Type_II_2025_redacted.pdf. Attachment (for Marissa's mailbox): SOC2_Type_II_2025.pdf (redacted). Scope note: report excludes customers running self-hosted private appliances; hosted inference and our control plane are in scope.

2) EU region behavior: For our Hosted EU offering (GCP eu-west1 / AWS eu-west-1 options) — data-at-rest (request logs, persisted embeddings, customer tenant storage) and the KV cache are provisioned in-region and are not replicated outside the selected cloud region by default. Background telemetry is aggregated to our EU telemetry cluster; PII is redacted before telemetry export. We will provide network flow diagrams on request.

3) Cross-border replication: Model checkpoints (weights) used by our hosted catalog are stored on regional object storage and are not automatically replicated cross-region unless specifically enabled for high-availability by the customer's account admin. For customers requiring strict no-export guarantees (e.g., ITAR), we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) which prevents any outbound replication.

4) OFAC/ITAR: Private deployment options exist — we support a dedicated VPC deployment and an on-prem appliance path for ITAR workloads. On-prem deployments can be air-gapped; for VPC deployments we can disable external replication and certify routing. Export-control compliance usually requires an export-classification questionnaire and, in some cases, legal review. We'll add standard language to the questionnaire answers.

Next steps: Marissa — I'll draft the highlighted questionnaire answers and attach the SOC2 redacted PDF. Also proposing a 30-minute technical call with Acme security this week to walk the procurement team through the architecture diagrams and replication guarantees.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
